title: Sufficient Unto the Day
subtitle: Before we take the argument apart, we rest inside its last line
teaser: This week has a whole argument to make — birds, flowers, a king, a garrison, a joy that doesn't wait. Today we don't make any of it. We sit inside where it lands.
theme: The last line of a bigger argument, held alone before the argument begins
framework: Matthew 6:34 - Today has enough trouble of its own

modules.passage: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.
redLetter: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.
emphasis: Today has enough trouble of its own
modules.scriptureContext: The closing line of a much longer teaching — the only line we sit with today.

modules.heading: One Line, Held Alone
modules.content:
This sentence is the last note of a much longer argument — ten verses about birds that don't farm, flowers that don't spin, a Father who already knows what His children need before they ask. The King James rendering gave it a phrase that outlived the sermon it came from: sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof. Whatever tomorrow holds, it is not today's to carry yet.

We're in the part of God's story called MINISTRY — Jesus, mid-sermon on a Galilean hillside, teaching kingdom life to ordinary people before the cross that would secure it. He taught this to people whose worry was not abstract — day laborers and small farmers, close enough to the edge that a bad harvest was a real threat, not a mood. He was not telling them nothing was wrong. He was telling them where the line falls: today's trouble belongs to today. Tomorrow's has not arrived, and will bring its own portion when it does, no earlier.

This week will take the fuller argument apart — a prophet fed by an unclean bird, a wildflower that outdresses a king, a peace that stands guard like a sentry, a joy commanded before the good news arrives. Today, none of that yet. It is Sunday. Sit inside the last line before the argument that built it begins.

modules.prompt: What piece of tomorrow have you already been carrying today, uninvited?

modules.heading: Sabbath

scripture_anchor.text: Today has enough trouble of its own.

modules.invitation: Sit somewhere quiet for five unhurried minutes. No study, no fixing, no rehearsing tomorrow. If a worry about tomorrow surfaces, name it once, and set it back down outside today's boundary. The silence is the practice.
modules.prayerText: Father, today is enough. I hand tomorrow back to You, unopened. Amen.
